name: Standing Calf Raise
description: The standing calf raise is a plantarflexion exercise performed with extended knees, emphasizing the gastrocnemius. It is typically performed on a calf raise machine or on the edge of a step, and is the primary exercise for developing calf size and plantar flexion strength.

execution.starting_position: Stand on the calf raise platform with the balls of the feet on the edge and heels hanging off. Shoulders under the pads. Knees straight but not locked.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust pad height so there is slight pressure on the shoulders. Keep knees nearly fully extended throughout.
steps: Lower the heels as far as possible below the platform for a maximum calf stretch.
Press up onto the toes as high as possible, fully contracting the calves.
Hold the peak position for one second, then lower under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom, missing the eccentric stretch benefit
Using a partial range of motion — go as far down and up as possible
Bending the knees, which shifts emphasis to the soleus
safety_considerations: Achilles tendon tightness is common — warm up well before heavy sets
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full plantar flexion at the top, full dorsiflexion stretch at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Full stretch at the bottom — let the heels drop all the way
Drive up onto the big toe side of the foot at the top
